title: “You Still Say ‘I Love God’… So Why Does He Feel So Far Away?”
paragraphs:
“You Still Say ‘I Love God’… So Why Does He Feel So Far Away?”
When Silence Feels Louder Than Your Prayers and Heaven Feels Closed
You didn’t stop loving God.
That’s what makes this so confusing.

You still whisper His name when things fall apart. You still pause when guilt creeps in. You still remember what it felt like when His presence was undeniable—when worship made your chest feel like it would burst, when Scripture felt alive, when even silence felt holy.
But now?
Now it feels like you’re talking into the void.
And the worst part is… you don’t know when it changed.

You didn’t wake up one morning and decide to drift. There was no dramatic rebellion, no loud rejection. Just small things. Quiet compromises. Subtle distractions. A slow fading. And now here you are, still calling Him “Lord,” but feeling like a stranger standing outside a locked door.
You love God… but you don’t feel close to Him anymore.
And that tension? It’s exhausting.
David knew this feeling. Not the polished, victorious king we like to quote—but the broken, desperate man who cried out in Psalm 22:1:

“אֵלִי אֵלִי לָמָה עֲזַבְתָּנִי”
Eli, Eli, lama azavtani
“My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?”
This wasn’t atheism.
This was intimacy in pain.
This was someone who knew God deeply… and yet felt abandoned.
And if that sounds familiar, you’re not alone—you’re human.
Even Jesus Himself stepped into that exact cry on the cross (Matthew 27:46), speaking in Aramaic:

“Ἠλί Ἠλί λιμὰ σαβαχθανί”
Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani
God in the flesh… feeling the distance.
Let that sink in.
Your struggle doesn’t disqualify you.
But it does reveal something deeper.
Because sometimes the distance you feel isn’t because God moved… but because something quietly stepped in between.
Isaiah 59:2 doesn’t whisper—it confronts:

“כִּי אִם־עֲוֹנֹתֵיכֶם הָיוּ מַבְדִּלִים בֵּינֵיכֶם לְבֵין אֱלֹהֵיכֶם”
“But your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God.”
Not because He stopped loving you.
But because sin numbs what once felt alive.
And here’s the part most people avoid…
Sometimes it’s not loud sin.
It’s tolerated sin.

It’s the things you justified.
The habits you said weren’t “that bad.”
The moments you knew the Holy Spirit nudged you… and you ignored it.
Not out of hatred for God.
But out of comfort.
And slowly… sensitivity fades.
You still believe.
You just don’t feel Him like before.
But listen carefully—this is where everything changes.
Because distance in feeling is not the same as distance in reality.
James 4:8 doesn’t say “wait until you feel close.”
It says:
“Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you.”
In Greek, “ἐγγίσατε τῷ Θεῷ” (engisate tō Theō) means to intentionally move closer—to make a conscious step, not an emotional reaction.
This isn’t about waiting for a feeling.
It’s about making a return.

Even when it feels dry.
Even when it feels fake.
Even when your prayers feel empty.
Because real love doesn’t disappear when emotions fade.
It fights to come back.
And maybe… just maybe… that ache you feel?
That discomfort?
That quiet dissatisfaction with your distance from Him?
That’s not rejection.
That’s invitation.
Because people who are truly lost don’t miss God.
But you do.
And that means something in you is still alive.
Revelation 2:4-5 says:
“You have abandoned the love you had at first… Remember therefore from where you have fallen; repent, and do the works you did at first.”
Not perform.
Not pretend.
Return.

Go back to the place where you were honest.
Where you didn’t hide.
Where you didn’t negotiate with sin.
Where Jesus wasn’t just part of your life… He was your life.
Because the truth is… you don’t need a new version of God.
You need a restored connection with the same God who never left.
And He’s not waiting with disappointment.
He’s waiting with open arms.
The kind of arms that carried a cross for you.
The kind of love that bled instead of walking away.
The kind of grace that rewrites stories no matter how far they’ve gone.
So if this hit something deep…
If you’ve been pretending you’re okay spiritually but you know something’s missing…
Be honest.
Someone reading your honesty might finally feel brave enough to stop pretending too.
Not to expose them—but to remind them they’re not alone.
Not because we need numbers.
But because you need consistent truth in a world that constantly pulls you away.
Because this isn’t just content.
This is rescue.
And maybe… this moment right now?
This quiet conviction you feel?
This is where your comeback begins.
You were never meant to love God from a distance.
